raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret “introduce our product to a new buyer” as a single acquisition email for a prospective developer-minded newsletter operator, not onboarding for an existing customer. The email should introduce Buttondown through one concrete use case—scheduling newsletter sends from the reader’s own code—and ask them to inspect the public implementation documentation.

intent.desired_action: Inspect Buttondown’s public API-scheduling documentation to decide whether its code-driven sending workflow fits.

raw_plan.reader: A developer-minded newsletter operator who wants control over how newsletter content is assembled and may prefer to drive sending from code rather than depend entirely on a web interface or fixed automation template.
raw_plan.reader_scope: Prospective developer-minded operators evaluating a code-driven newsletter workflow. Do not assume a specific programming language, hosting environment, spreadsheet, integration, current provider, or prior failed implementation.
raw_plan.promise: Buttondown can serve as the sending layer behind a newsletter workflow the reader controls in code: its API can schedule newsletter emails, and API access is available on the free plan.
raw_plan.orientation: Buttondown is an email newsletter platform that lets developer-minded operators create, schedule, and send newsletter emails through an API.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move the reader from seeing Buttondown as another newsletter interface to understanding one concrete, documented use: scheduling a newsletter send from their own code, then inspecting the exact mechanism before signing up.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single-email acquisition campaign needs one complete reason to want Buttondown, not a catalogue. API scheduling is the strongest fit for this solution-aware audience: it supports control over newsletter assembly, has a concrete implementation mechanism, and is available on the free plan. The public scheduling documentation is the appropriate first step because it lets a developer inspect the request and conditions before creating an account. No customer proof is used because the licensed campaign boundary does not establish any named customer or outcome claim. Which customers or quotes may we name?

emails.selection_reason: This audience wants control over how newsletter content is assembled and includes budget-conscious operators. The documented scheduling API gives them a concrete way to connect their own logic to newsletter delivery, while free-plan API access lowers the commercial barrier without becoming the main proposition.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the reader assembles newsletters in their own code, they can keep that logic there and use Buttondown’s API to schedule the resulting newsletter email for delivery.
value_case.mechanism: A script authenticates with a Buttondown API token and posts an email to /v1/emails with its status and publish_date set for the scheduled send.
decision_conditions: The reader must supply and run the code that prepares and submits the request.
Requests require a Buttondown API token.
API access, including API scheduling, is available on the free plan.

claim_conditions: Authenticate the API request with a Buttondown token.
Set the email’s status and publish_date to schedule it.
The reader remains responsible for the external automation logic and trigger.
emails.target_audience: Developer-minded newsletter operators evaluating a code-driven way to schedule newsletter sends.
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect Buttondown’s documented scheduling request and decide whether it fits the newsletter workflow they want to control in code.
emails.single_idea: Buttondown can take a newsletter produced by the reader’s own code and schedule its send through a documented API request, with API access available on the free plan.
emails.felt_need: I want control over how my newsletter is assembled, and I need the sending step to work with code rather than force the whole workflow into a fixed template.
emails.mechanism: Buttondown documents POST /v1/emails for creating an email. Supplying status and publish_date schedules the send; the request authenticates with an API token.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: For a developer-minded operator, being able to retrieve newsletter content in ordinary file formats is a distinct reason to consider the platform. The public export documentation answers that control question before adoption.

value_case.reader_benefit: The operator can retrieve their Buttondown email records and message contents as files they can inspect and store outside the dashboard.
value_case.mechanism: Starting an email export from the Emails tab downloads a CSV and a folder containing each email’s contents as Markdown files.
decision_conditions: The export is initiated from the Emails tab in the Buttondown dashboard.
The documented mechanism covers email content; it does not establish a complete export of every kind of account or engagement data.

claim_conditions: Describe the output specifically as a CSV plus email contents in Markdown files.
Do not characterize the export as self-hosting, legal ownership, or a complete platform backup.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: Buttondown provides a documented way to download email data as a CSV and each email’s contents as Markdown files.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: From the Emails tab, the operator initiates an export that downloads a CSV and a folder of Markdown files containing the emails.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: adopting a newsletter platform may mean leaving published email content accessible only through its interface. After: Buttondown documents a file-based email export whose exact contents can be inspected before adoption.
must_not_say: That the export proves outright ownership of the archive.
That it is a complete backup of subscribers, engagement data, consent records, settings, or the entire account.
That exported content becomes independently hosted.
That the export guarantees an easy or lossless migration to another provider.
alternative_arguments.objection: If I publish my newsletter there, can I retrieve the email content in ordinary files?
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Review Buttondown’s documented email export format.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented CSV-and-Markdown export provides acceptable access to newsletter email content.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The documentation shows that an email export downloads a CSV plus a folder containing each email’s contents as Markdown files.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page does not establish legal ownership, retention rights, a complete account backup, or export coverage for subscriber engagement and consent data.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete CSV-and-Markdown export rather than broad claims about ownership, portability, or avoiding lock-in.

The documented mechanism covers email content; it does not establish a complete export of every kind of account or engagement data.

claim_conditions: Describe the output specifically as a CSV plus email contents in Markdown files.
Do not characterize the export as self-hosting, legal ownership, or a complete platform backup.
Authenticate requests with a Buttondown API token in the Authorization header (R12).
Set the email's status and publish_date fields to schedule a send, or update a draft's status to 'about_to_send' to dispatch it (R14, R15).
Create a webhook for the specific event and point its URL at your own application to react to Buttondown events (R6).
Use the CSV-file imports endpoint for bulk subscriber loads rather than per-subscriber POSTs (R10).

The stated mechanism is an API, and it is documented for drafting, scheduling, sending and subscriber creation, but the named tools have no documented native connectors — those links depend on generic API, webhook or Zapier use (R7, R6) — and programmatic subscriber creation is capped at 100/day by default with CSV import as the documented bulk path (R16, R10).
alternative_arguments.single_idea: Buttondown provides a documented way to download email data as a CSV and each email’s contents as Markdown files.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: From the Emails tab, the operator initiates an export that downloads a CSV and a folder of Markdown files containing the emails.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: adopting a newsletter platform may mean leaving published email content accessible only through its interface. After: Buttondown documents a file-based email export whose exact contents can be inspected before adoption.
must_not_say: That the export proves outright ownership of the archive.
That it is a complete backup of subscribers, engagement data, consent records, settings, or the entire account.
That exported content becomes independently hosted.
That the export guarantees an easy or lossless migration to another provider.
alternative_arguments.objection: If I publish my newsletter there, can I retrieve the email content in ordinary files?
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented CSV-and-Markdown export provides acceptable access to newsletter email content.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The official page documents this verified fact: Buttondown documents an email export mechanism that downloads a CSV plus a folder containing the contents of each email as Markdown files.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page does not establish legal ownership, retention rights, a complete account backup, or export coverage for subscriber engagement and consent data.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete CSV-and-Markdown export rather than broad claims about ownership, portability, or avoiding lock-in.

events.body:
Build the newsletter in your own code, then schedule its delivery through Buttondown.

Buttondown is an email newsletter platform for creating, scheduling, and sending emails through an API. Your code stays in charge of how the content comes together.

When your script is ready, authenticate with a Buttondown API token and post the email to `/v1/emails`. Add `status: scheduled` and a future `publish_date` to set the send time.

API access, including scheduling, is available on the free plan. Buttondown handles the scheduled newsletter send after your own code prepares and submits the request.

The official documentation shows the request in Python, Ruby, JavaScript, and cURL, so you can see whether it fits the workflow you want to run.
